recall.minute: Command-query separation says a method either acts or answers; CQRS lifts this to architecture, with command handling writing to a write store and query handling reading a separate read store updated by projections, which removes contention and simplifies permissions but makes the system eventually consistent. In ML, the command side updates data, features and models while the query side serves predictions, metrics and dashboards, connected by event streams, brokers or asynchronous pipelines; a new model version reaches all endpoints within minutes. RAG grounds LLM answers in external data: an ingestion pipeline extracts, chunks, embeds and indexes documents into a vector store, and a query pipeline embeds the question, searches, retrieves context and builds the prompt, so RAG is pipe-and-filter plus CQRS. Frameworks such as LangChain, embeddings such as Sentence-BERT, and stores such as Chroma with HNSW indexes implement it. Monoliths deploy everything together and are simple but hard to scale and evolve; microservices follow the single-responsibility principle, scale and deploy independently, and for ML split gateway, model and logging services.
